mission.statement: Build a finished, beautiful, playable cel-shaded arcade boat racing game in Three.js on an infinite open ocean.
mission.firstExperience: A clean install and development launch drops the player directly into a four-boat race.

factory.area: New Three.js game repository covering rendering, ocean simulation, race systems, AI, riders, HUD, camera, audio, and performance.

constraints.text: Use Vite, Three.js r1xx, TypeScript, and ES modules, runnable with npm install and npm run dev.
Use no downloaded models, textures, HDRIs, or audio; generate every mesh, texture, and sound in code.
Target Chrome on a MacBook M5 Pro at retina resolution and a solid 60fps.
Use instancing, frustum culling, adaptive pixel ratio, and an LOD scheme.
The complete game uses a coherent high-saturation palette across water, sky, hulls, riders, and UI.

antiGoals.text: No physically based visual treatment or real cubemap environment probes.
No externally downloaded binary art or audio assets.
No static decal-only foam, rigid riders, default-looking HTML HUD, or glass-like boat handling.
Add automated checks that reject PBR materials, runtime external asset fetches, and prohibited binary source assets.

protectedCapabilities.text: Water banding, foam, wakes, spray, and sparkle remain a first-class visual system.
Cel lighting and outline consistency remain visually dominant and free of doubled edges.
Riders remain lively, physics-driven characters rather than rigid props.
Frame pacing on target hardware remains a release requirement.

requirements.text: Render 3-4 discrete diffuse lighting bands with nearest-filtered ramp sampling.
Render view-distance-scaled inverted-hull outlines on boats, riders, buoys, and gates.
Render screen-space interior edges from normal and depth discontinuities without doubling hull silhouettes.
Apply Fresnel rim light to every rider and boat.
Render hard-edged banded specular highlights using a ramp or matcap rather than a real environment probe.
Render a gradient sky dome, hard-rimmed drifting cel clouds, and a graphic sun flare using the canonical palette.
Displace the ocean with 4-6 Gerstner waves combining swell and chop with crest sharpening.
Provide an infinite recentred or projected ocean without visible seams, repetition, or LOD popping.
Band water color by height and depth into hard deep, mid, and crest tones.
Render crest foam, hull foam rings, persistent spreading wakes, and spray from hard landings and turns.
Render animated quantized sparkle highlights that read as anime glitter.
Run four-boat, three-lap races with countdown, finish line, times, placement, and results screen.
Provide a closed wave-following spline course with racing ribbon, checkpoint gates, wrong-way detection, corner preview, straights, hairpin, sweeper, chicane, and cross-swell airtime section.
Simulate boat buoyancy at 5-6 hull points with throttle, speed-sensitive steering, drift boost, airtime, pitch, roll, and landing impacts.
Drive three AI racers along the spline with distinct personalities, mild rubber-banding, avoidance, and occasional mistakes.
Animate a procedural rider on every boat with turn lean, acceleration weight shift, working arms, landing crouch, wave-synced idle bob, and finish celebration.
Make rider silhouettes and poses visibly respond to boat physics rather than remain rigid.
Provide a spring-damped chase camera, speed FOV kick, capped landing shake, and cinematic countdown/results orbit.
Display a cel-styled speedometer, lap, position, split times, boost, and minimap with all racers.
Synthesize engine, water rush, impact, and start-horn audio with Web Audio.
A clean npm install followed by npm run dev launches a playable race in Chrome.
The repository contains and fetches no prohibited external art or audio assets.
The target MacBook M5 Pro sustains the agreed 60fps frame-pacing budget at retina resolution in the stress scenario.
Every important visual claim is backed by deterministic Playwright captures from stable camera states.
Temporal visual systems are verified with time-separated deterministic frames or clips, not screenshots alone.
Simulation uses a fixed timestep and seeded randomness so critic evidence can be reproduced.
Every milestone remains runnable and records honest subsystem quality and named defects.
The repository includes a README, clean architecture, and readable shader code explaining tunable thresholds.
Automated checks reject PBR materials, external runtime fetches, and prohibited binary source assets.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A clean install and npm run dev launches a playable four-boat race.
The art and audio pipeline contains no prohibited external assets or PBR rendering path.
Canonical visual evidence shows deliberate cel bands, consistent outlines, interior edges without doubling, rim light, banded specular, and a coherent sky palette.
Water evidence shows Gerstner motion, infinite coverage, hard color bands, all four foam components, and quantized sparkle without visible repetition or seams.
The course and race lifecycle correctly enforce checkpoints, laps, wrong-way state, finish results, and HUD state for all four racers.
The player boat visibly responds to the shared wave field and the user accepts its throttle, steering, drift, airtime, and landing feel.
All AI personalities complete deterministic races with avoidance, bounded rubber-banding, and seeded mistakes.
Every rider visibly leans, shifts, works controls, crouches, bobs, and celebrates in response to simulation state.
Camera, HUD, and synthesized audio provide all named race feedback without obscuring play.
Every milestone remains runnable and preserves screenshots, named defects, and honest quality status.
The target MacBook M5 Pro passes the approved frame-pacing budget in the canonical stress scene.
Documentation, clean architecture, shared contracts, and deterministic validation remain green at completion.

humanCriteria.question: Does the water read as energetic anime art rather than a tiled or smoothly shaded surface?
Does the boat feel weighty and responsive without reading as motion over glass?
Do riders visibly carry turning, acceleration, wave, and landing loads?
Do sky, water, boats, riders, particles, and HUD read as one deliberate palette?
